learning_outcomes.text: Be able to perform teamwork applying the knowledge acquired in the Thermal Engineering course.
Be able to solve problems related to thermal engineering, posed during the course.
Be able to write and defend a work in the field of thermal engineering.
Be able to autonomously learn topics related to thermal engineering.
Be able to explain, relate and differentiate the three basic mechanisms of heat transfer.
Be able to apply the different parameters and methods for solving problems in radiation.
Be able to practically apply thermal insulation methods and enhance heat exchange by adding extended surfaces.
Be able to represent different reversible cycles, as well as ideal power and vapor compression cycles, on a thermodynamic diagram.
Be able to relate, classify and apply the fundamentals of thermodynamics to open systems.
Be able to understand the meaning of the main thermal parameters associated with conduction and know how to apply them to obtain the temperature field in simple and composite geometries.

Be able to understand the heat transfer mechanism by convection, the expressions describing the phenomenon according to the configuration used and the characteristics of the fluid, and the dimensionless numbers used in convection.

syllabus_topics: 1.1. Introduction to heat transfer mechanisms and fundamental laws.
2.1. Fundamentals of heat transfer by conduction.
5.2. Heat transfer by radiation. Calculation methods.
P.1. Measurement elements in thermal engineering.
P.2. Limitation of energy consumption in buildings.
teaching_methods: Problem-solving exercises (Resolución de ejercicios y problemas)
Use of multimedia presentations with blackboard developments
Laboratory sessions with didactic installations and specific software
assessment_rules: To pass the course, a global grade of at least 5 out of 10 is required, and the final exam score must be at least 4 out of 10. If the final exam score is below 4, the overall grade will be solely the final exam score. For the second ordinary call, continuous assessment only includes laboratory reports (15%) and is not recoverable, with the final exam accounting for 85%. For the extraordinary call, the final exam accounts for 100% and has no minimum score. Fraudulent activity in any assessment will result in a 0 for that activity or exam.
